questions.text: As per the table below, what is the percentage increase in the number of female employees from 2019 to 2021? Year | Total Employees | Male Employees | Female Employees 2019 | 500 | 300 | 200 2020 | 600 | 350 | 250 2021 | 720 | 400 | 320
questions.solution: Shortcut: Female 2019 = 200, Female 2021 = 320. Increase = 120. % Increase = (120/200) × 100 = 60%. (Option check: 50% of 200 = 100 → 300; 65% = 130 → 330). Full: Number of female employees in 2019 = 200. In 2021 = 320. Increase = 320 - 200 = 120. Percentage Increase = (Increase / Original Value) × 100 = (120 / 200) × 100 = 60%.

questions.text: Given below are two sentences. Which of the given starters can combine the two sentences into a single sentence without changing the meaning? (I) The RBI kept the repo rate unchanged for the eighth consecutive time. (II) The central bank remains focused on withdrawal of accommodation to control inflation. Starters: 1. Despite keeping the repo rate unchanged... 2. Because the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged... 3. As the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged...
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the logical relationship. Sentence I (Status quo) vs Sentence II (Hawkish action/intent) shows CONTRAST. 'Despite' signals contrast. 'Because' and 'As' signal cause/effect. Keeping rates unchanged is not the CAUSE for focusing on withdrawal. Step-by-step: 1. Analyze logic: Rate pause (I) vs Tightening stance (II) = Contrast. 2. Starter 1 ('Despite') correctly establishes contrast: 'Despite keeping the repo rate unchanged..., the central bank remains focused...'. 3. Starter 2 ('Because') implies causation (incorrect logic). 4. Starter 3 ('As') implies causation or time (incorrect logic). Only Starter 1 works.

questions.text: A can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B can complete the same work in 20 days. They work together for 4 days and then leave. What fraction of the work is left?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Take total work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units. A's efficiency = 4 units/day, B's = 3 units/day. Combined = 7 units/day. Work done in 4 days = 28 units. Remaining = 32 units. Fraction left = 32/60 = 8/15. Full: 1 day work of A = 1/15, B = 1/20. Together = 7/60. In 4 days = 28/60 = 7/15. Work left = 1 - 7/15 = 8/15.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill the blank in the given sentence so that it makes both grammatical and contextual sense. The audit committee has decided to _______ the discrepancies found in the annual financial report.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use **collocation elimination** with the object 'discrepancies'. 'Look after' collocates with people/property (care), 'look out for' with dangers/opportunities (vigilance), and 'look down upon' with people/behaviour (disdain). Only 'look into' collocates with matters/issues/discrepancies meaning 'investigate'. Full Solution: The context implies the committee will examine the discrepancies already found. 'Look into' means to investigate. 'Look after' means to take care of. 'Look out for' means to watch for. 'Look down upon' means to regard with contempt. Only option A fits the context of a formal investigation.

questions.text: Rahul starts walking from point X. He walks 10 m North, turns right and walks 15 m, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left again and walks 15 m to reach point Y. What is the shortest distance between X and Y?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Opposite equal displacements cancel. East 15 m and West 15 m cancel out. Net movement is North 10 m + North 10 m = 20 m North. Distance = 20 m. Full: Plot coordinates: Start (0,0). N10 → (0,10). Right(E)15 → (15,10). Left(N)10 → (15,20). Left(W)15 → (0,20). Distance from (0,0) to (0,20) = 20 m.

questions.text: Match the sentence halves in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form grammatically and contextually correct sentences. **Column 1** A. The new policy aims to reduce carbon emissions B. Despite the heavy rainfall C. The committee has decided to postpone the event D. Had the students prepared well **Column 2** 1. they would have passed the examination with flying colours. 2. the match continued without any interruption. 3. by promoting renewable energy sources across the country. 4. due to the unforeseen circumstances arising suddenly.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the 'Had...' starter (D) which mandates a Third Conditional ending ('would have...') — only Option 1 fits. This locks D-1. Check Option A for purpose ('aims to' + 'by + ing') -> Option 3. Check Option B for contrast ('Despite' + main clause) -> Option 2. Remaining C-4 fits reason ('decided to postpone' + 'due to'). Only Option A satisfies all. Worked Solution: D starts with 'Had' (Past Perfect), requiring a Perfect Conditional ('would have + V3') — matches only with 1. A ('aims to') pairs with purpose phrase 'by promoting' (3). B ('Despite') pairs with contrasting main clause 'the match continued' (2). C ('has decided to postpone') pairs with reason phrase 'due to' (4). Correct matching: A-3, B-2, C-4, D-1.

questions.text: A boat takes 8 hours to travel a certain distance upstream and 6 hours to travel the same distance downstream. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Ratio Method): Upstream Time : Downstream Time = 8 : 6 = 4 : 3. Since distance is constant, Speed Ratio (Up:Down) = 3 : 4. Let upstream speed = 3x, downstream speed = 4x. Speed of stream = (Down - Up)/2 = (4x - 3x)/2 = x/2. Given x/2 = 2 => x = 4. Speed of boat in still water = (Up + Down)/2 = (3x + 4x)/2 = 3.5x = 14 km/h. Full Method: Let boat speed = u, stream = 2. Distance = (u-2)*8 = (u+2)*6 => 8u - 16 = 6u + 12 => 2u = 28 => u = 14 km/h.

questions.text: In a certain code language: 'bank exam preparation' is coded as 'tp rm jk' 'preparation strategy guide' is coded as 'jk ln op' 'exam guide material' is coded as 'rm op qr' What is the code for 'strategy'?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Intersection Method. Compare Sentence 1 & 2: Common word 'preparation' = Common code 'jk'. Compare 1 & 3: Common word 'exam' = Common code 'rm'. Compare 2 & 3: Common word 'guide' = Common code 'op'. In Sentence 2, remaining word 'strategy' = remaining code 'ln'. Full Solution: Preparation = jk, Exam = rm, Guide = op. Bank = tp (from S1). Material = qr (from S3). Strategy = ln (from S2).

questions.text: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The letter of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is (D). (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.) The manager, along with his team members, is working late to finish the project before the deadline, but they are tired.

options.label: A
options.text: The manager, along with his team members,

options.label: B
options.text: is working late to finish the project before the deadline,

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the true subject ('The manager') and ignore the additive phrase ('along with...'). The subject is singular, so the pronoun in the final clause must be singular ('he is'), not plural ('they are'). Step-by-step: Part A introduces the singular subject 'The manager'. Part B correctly uses the singular verb 'is working' agreeing with the singular subject. Part C introduces a contrast clause with the plural pronoun 'they', which incorrectly refers back to the singular 'manager'. The error lies in Part C.

questions.text: Read the passage and answer the question that follows. "The shift towards green energy is often portrayed as a binary choice between fossil fuels and renewables. However, energy experts argue that the transition requires a nuanced approach, integrating bridge fuels like natural gas to ensure grid stability while storage technology matures. Ignoring this interim necessity risks energy poverty in developing nations." Which of the following can be logically inferred from the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Fossil fuels are superior to renewables for grid stability.

options.label: B
options.text: Natural gas is a permanent replacement for coal in the energy mix.

options.label: C
options.text: Current storage technology is fully capable of handling renewable intermittency.

options.label: D
options.text: A rapid transition to renewables without bridge fuels may harm developing economies.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate extremes/contradictions. Option A: 'Superior' is extreme; passage says 'bridge fuels... ensure stability', not superiority. Option B: 'Permanent' contradicts 'interim necessity' and 'bridge fuels'. Option C: 'Fully capable' contradicts 'while storage technology matures'. Option D: Aligns perfectly with 'Ignoring this interim necessity risks energy poverty'. Worked Solution: The passage explicitly states that ignoring the need for bridge fuels (interim necessity) risks energy poverty in developing nations. This directly supports Option D. Options A, B, and C contradict the passage's emphasis on 'nuanced approach', 'interim necessity', and technology 'maturing' (not mature).

questions.text: A is the brother of B. C is the father of A. D is the sister of C. How is D related to B?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Draw a quick family tree – C is father of A and B; D is sister of C, so D is the aunt of B. Step‑by‑step: C father of A ⇒ C father of B (since A and B are siblings). D sister of C ⇒ D is sibling of B's father ⇒ D is B's aunt.

questions.text: The perimeter of a rectangle is equal to the circumference of a circle of radius 14 cm. If the length of the rectangle is 24 cm, what is the area of the rectangle? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Circle circumference = 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 88 cm. Rectangle Perimeter = 88 = 2(L+B) → 24+B=44 → B=20 cm. Area = 24 × 20 = 480 cm². Full: Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 88 cm. Perimeter of rectangle = 2(24 + b) = 88 → b = 20 cm. Area = Length × Breadth = 24 × 20 = 480 cm².

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'EXAM' is written as 'FYBN' and 'TEST' is written as 'UFTU'. How will 'QUIZ' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check first letter shift: E→F (+1), T→U (+1). Apply +1 to each letter of QUIZ: Q→R, U→V, I→J, Z→A → RVJA. Full: Pattern is each letter replaced by next alphabetical letter (cyclic). E(5)→F(6), X(24)→Y(25), A(1)→B(2), M(13)→N(14). T(20)→U(21), E(5)→F(6), S(19)→T(20), T(20)→U(21). Q(17)→R(18), U(21)→V(22), I(9)→J(10), Z(26)→A(1).

questions.text: A train 240 metres long crosses a platform 360 metres long in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total distance = 240 + 360 = 600 m. Speed in m/s = 600/30 = 20 m/s. Convert to km/h by multiplying by 18/5 (or 3.6): 20 × 3.6 = 72 km/h. Full Method: Distance covered = Length of train + Length of platform = 600 m. Time = 30 s. Speed = Distance/Time = 20 m/s. 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h. Speed = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.text: Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H sit around a square table with two persons on each side facing the centre. A sits opposite C. B sits second to the right of A. D sits immediately to the left of B. Who sits opposite D?
questions.solution: If A is at position 1, C is at 5 (opposite). B is second to the right of A, placing B at position 4. D is immediately left of B, placing D at position 3. The person opposite D (position 3) is at position 7, which corresponds to E based on the remaining positions.
